summary.text: St. Solomon, son of St. David, is remembered as king, temple builder and a figure associated with biblical wisdom.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: St. Solomon succeeds his father, St. David, as king. First Kings describes the contested succession and the establishment of his reign. When asked what he desires, he requests understanding to govern the people, rather than wealth or victory over enemies.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: His reign includes the construction and dedication of the Temple at Jerusalem. The biblical narrative also describes royal wealth, international contacts and judgments associated with wisdom. It does not hide his failure: First Kings says that his many wives turn his heart toward other gods and records God’s judgment concerning the kingdom. His Orthodox commemoration should not erase this part of Scripture.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: First Kings reports a reign of forty years, his death and burial in the city of his father. The text does not describe martyrdom. This profile does not add an unverified story about his final repentance or cause of death.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA calls him Prophet-King and associates him with Proverbs, the Song of Songs and the Wisdom of Solomon. It distinguishes traditional attribution from the composition and transmission of all the material. His commemoration is among the Forefathers.
blocks.locator: Sole biographical paragraph and named Forefathers entry
